summary: Verified fix for FCM race condition (pushNotifications.js) + new /api/fcm/diagnostics/{user_id} endpoint. 19/19 backend regression tests pass against public URL, covering: health, admin login (email_or_phone/HeartLink@2026), /api/admin/push/status (provider=fcm, configured=true, can_send_notifications=true), /api/admin/push/test, /api/admin/push/send target=all, /api/fcm/register-token (valid + 404 for unknown user), NEW /api/fcm/diagnostics/{user_id} (returns user info + firebase_initialized=true + in_app_notification_count, 404 for unknown user, has_fcm_token=true + fcm_token_prefix + fcm_token_updated_at + test_send_result populated after register), backward-compat /api/admin/onesignal/{status,send,test}, /api/admin/daily-notification-status (scheduler_running=true), /api/admin/notifications/templates, /api/notifications/{user_id}. Frontend source verification: (a) all 4 addListener calls (registration, registrationError, pushNotificationReceived, pushNotificationActionPerformed) appear BEFORE PushNotifications.register() call — race condition confirmed fixed at lines 56-77 with register() at line 94; (b) registerTokenWithBackend has 3-attempt retry with 2s/4s backoff + localStorage diagnostics writes; (c) no oneSignalService/OneSignal references remain. Frontend loads cleanly (title 'HeartLink - India's #1 Safe Dating App...'), 0 console/page errors, no window.OneSignal global, webpack compiles (only non-blocking source-map warnings for @capacitor-community/admob & google-auth).

The endpoint will start returning success=true once real Android devices register post-fix. Consider adding a UI/admin banner: 'X real users have FCM tokens; Y are pending first Android app open post-fix'.

Optional: rename NotificationManager.jsx handlers from OneSignal→FCM for UI clarity (backward-compat endpoints still work).
critical_code_review_comments: pushNotifications.js fix is correct: PushNotifications.removeAllListeners() + all 4 addListener() calls now precede PushNotifications.register(). Retry loop (3x with linear backoff 2s/4s) in registerTokenWithBackend guards against transient network failure at boot.
/api/fcm/diagnostics/{user_id} correctly excludes _id in projection, returns 404 for unknown users, and only invokes test_send when a token exists. Good separation.
/api/admin/push/send still has the pre-existing quirk noted in iteration_12: when target='user_ids' it runs admin_broadcast first then overrides — unrelated to this fix but worth revisiting.

fcm_service.send_to_all excludes AI profiles but /api/admin/push/status count query does not — the users_with_fcm_token metric can therefore over-report vs actual send targets. Minor inconsistency.

Added 7 new tests covering /api/fcm/diagnostics/{user_id} endpoint + pushNotifications.js source-structure assertions (race-condition fix). push_test/push_send_all tests now tolerate no_tokens shape since real users have zero FCM tokens post-cleanup (per RCA). Verify success=true on these endpoints only after real Android devices come online with the fixed pushNotifications.js and register tokens.
rca of the issue: Root cause confirmed and fixed: In /app/frontend/src/services/pushNotifications.js, PushNotifications.register() was previously invoked BEFORE the 'registration' event listener was attached, so FCM's synchronous token callback fired into the void and was never captured or POSTed to /api/fcm/register-token. Consequence: fcm_token remained empty on every real user, and every server-side send_to_user/send_to_all short-circuited with error='no_token'. Fix (verified by automated source assertions): removeAllListeners() + 4 addListener() calls now precede register(); registerTokenWithBackend gained a 3-attempt retry with 2s/4s backoff + localStorage diagnostics. New /api/fcm/diagnostics/{user_id} endpoint enables live inspection (has_fcm_token, prefix, updated_at, firebase_initialized, test_send_result). Mitigation: users must reopen the Android app once post-fix to trigger registration; monitor users_with_fcm_token count trend via /api/admin/push/status.
